sources.title: April 2015 Nepal earthquake
sources.observation: The article reports that the April 2015 Nepal earthquake (Mw 7.8–7.9) had a shallow hypocenter of about 8.2 km and was followed by frequent aftershocks, including Mw 6.7 the next day and Mw 7.3 on May 12. It states that geophysicists and other experts had warned for decades that Nepal was vulnerable to a deadly earthquake, particularly because of its geology, urbanization, and architecture.

sources.title: The physics of earthquakes
sources.observation: The authors state that earthquakes occur as a result of global plate motion, while noting that this simple picture is incomplete. They add that some plate boundaries glide smoothly but others experience catastrophic failures, and that earthquakes can sometimes be triggered by other large earthquakes thousands of kilometers away.
